content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Overestimates in late forecast period (last 5–10 days) when prices show downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Overreacts to recent high prices, overshooting downward corrections.
- Underreacts to sustained low prices, failing to anticipate mean reversion or rebound.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in periods of high volatility or rapid price shifts.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to reduce forecast below recent low, often holding too high.
- Forecast tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating short-term spikes and overestimating long-term trends.
- In multi-day forecast, model often fails to capture the true price’s “tail” — the final 3–5 days are frequently overestimated.
